```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(data.table)
BY <- 2023
run <- "run60" 
save.output <- TRUE
```

This document describes a methodology designed for deriving households at risk of displacement due to land use zoning. It is one of many components of the displacement index measure (for details on the overall measure, ask Brian or Mary).

In the past, using results from residential structures built in a simulation were compared to structures in the base year. Here, the the measure is not dependent on a specific simulation. Instead, a set of rules is applied to the base year data `r BY`. We are using an updated FLU, finalized in September 2026.


## Inputs and Code

This R markdown file is located in the [displacement GitHub repo]( https://github.com/psrc/urbansimRtools/blob/master/displacement/BY2023/displacement_risk.Rmd). 

Input data are csv files exported from run `r substr(run, nchar(run)-1, nchar(run))`. Note that only data in the baseyear and development project proposals created in the first year are needed, which would be the same for any run. Thus, the method is not dependent on simulation results. The only run-dependent factor is how the re-development filter is set. 

The following datasets are needed:

* `r BY`/buildings.csv
* `r BY`/parcels.csv
* `r BY`/households.csv
* `r BY`/census_blocks.csv
* `r BY`/census_block_groups.csv
* `r BY`/development_project_proposals.csv (MPDs)
* `r BY + 1`/development_project_proposals.csv
* `r BY + 1`/development_project_proposal_components.csv


## Data Cleaning and Filtering

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# load data
pcl <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "parcels.csv"))
setkey(pcl, parcel_id)
bld <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "buildings.csv"))
setkey(bld, building_id)
hh <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "households.csv"))[building_id > 0]
setkey(hh, building_id)
hh[bld, parcel_id := i.parcel_id] # assign parcel to households
cblocks <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "census_blocks.csv"))
cbgs <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "census_block_groups.csv"))
# assign census tracts to parcels
pcl[cblocks[cbgs, census_tract_id := i.census_tract_id, on = "census_block_group_id"], 
    census_tract_id := i.census_tract_id, on = "census_block_id"]
# load development proposals
mpd <- fread(file.path(run, BY, "development_project_proposals.csv"))
dprop <- fread(file.path(run, BY + 1, "development_project_proposals.csv"))
setkey(dprop, proposal_id)
cdprop <- fread(file.path(run, BY + 1, "development_project_proposal_components.csv"))
setkey(cdprop, proposal_id, parcel_id)

# remove projects on parcels where there are MPDs
devmpd <- mpd[start_year <= BY + 3]
dprop <- dprop[!parcel_id %in% devmpd[,parcel_id]]
mpd <- mpd[start_year > BY + 3]

# fix related to an issue of creating new development projects 
# due to land_area for existing buildings being 0
dprop[bld[, .(is_redevelopment = 0, .N), by = parcel_id], has_bld := i.N > 0, on = c("parcel_id", "is_redevelopment")][is.na(has_bld), has_bld := FALSE]
dprop <- dprop[is_redevelopment == 1 | !has_bld]

# join components with proposals
cdprop <- cdprop[proposal_id %in% dprop[, proposal_id]]
cdprop[dprop, parcel_id := i.parcel_id]
```

* Remove MPDs with start year smaller than `r BY + 4`. Development projects on these parcels will not be considered. It affects `r nrow(devmpd[, .N, by = parcel_id])` parcels. *Here we are assuming that the removed MPDs are already built and therefore households on these parcels are not at risk.*  

<!--* Some building records have unrealistically large year built, so we replace it with 0 and treat the year built in these records as missing. Specifically, `r nrow(bld[year_built > BY + 2])` buildings have `year_built > ` `r BY + 2` and thus are set to `year_built = 0`.-->

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# correct wrong year_built
bld[year_built > BY + 2, year_built := 0]
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# select occupied residential buildings that are older than 10 years
age.limit <- 8
rbld <- bld[residential_units > 0 & building_id %in% hh[, building_id] & year_built < (BY + 2 - age.limit)]

# exclude parcels that are tax exempt
rbld <- rbld[not_demolish == 0 & !parcel_id %in% pcl[exemption == 1, parcel_id]]

# select proposals that are on parcels with selected residential buildings
redprop <- dprop[parcel_id %in% rbld[, parcel_id]]
setkey(redprop, proposal_id, parcel_id)

# select buildings that are on parcels that have at least one proposal
redbld <- rbld[parcel_id %in% redprop[, parcel_id]]
setkey(redbld, building_id, parcel_id)
```

* Use only buildings that:
    * have residential units,
    * are occupied by a household,
    * are older than `r age.limit` years (*here assuming that buildings less than about 8 years old are too young to destroy; also, the value of 8 is used in the re-development filter of the simulation run*),
    * are not on a tax-exempt parcel (*owned by government, churches, nonprofits or housing authorities*), and
    * there is a development proposal on its parcel.

    Result: `r nrow(redbld)` buildings on `r nrow(redbld[, .N, by = parcel_id])` parcels
    
* Use only development proposals that are on parcels with buildings selected in the previous step: `r nrow(redprop)` proposals on `r nrow(redprop[, .N, by = parcel_id])` parcels

## Method

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# mark residential and non-res proposals
proptype <- cdprop[proposal_id %in% redprop[, proposal_id]][, 
                            .(is_res = any(building_type_id %in% c(19, 4, 12)), 
                                is_nonres = any(!building_type_id %in% c(19, 4, 12))), by = proposal_id]
setkey(proptype, proposal_id)
redprop <- merge(redprop, proptype, by = "proposal_id")

# for non-res proposals, estimate the number of units as if the project would be MF residential
redprop[, units_est := units_proposed]
redprop[is_nonres == TRUE, units_est := round(units_proposed/1000)]
```

1. For non-residential development proposals, convert proposed sqft into dwelling units using a conversion ratio of 1000 sqft per unit (typical for multi-family units). The idea is that it gives a rough approximation of the size of the proposed structure, in order to assess if it is larger than the existing structure, and thus is likely to be built. 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# select only the largest proposals
redprop[redprop[, .I[which.max(units_est)], by = parcel_id]$V1, is_max := TRUE]
redpropm <- redprop[!is.na(is_max) & is_max == TRUE]
```

2. Determine the largest proposal per parcel measured on the proposed or estimated dwelling units. 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# sum existing DUs for each of the affected parcels
redpcl <- redbld[, .(DU = sum(residential_units)), by = parcel_id]
setkey(redpcl, parcel_id)

# join with existing units
redpropm[redpcl, existing_units := i.DU, on = "parcel_id"]
```

3. Sum the number of existing dwelling units for each of the `r nrow(redpcl)` parcels.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# select proposals where the number of proposed units is 1 times of the existing units, 
# or if MPD, proposed should be simply larger than existing 
comp.factor <- 1
redpropm.build <- redpropm[units_est > comp.factor*existing_units | (units_est > existing_units & parcel_id %in% mpd[, parcel_id])]
```

4. Select parcels where the number of proposed units is (strictly) `r comp.factor ` time(s) larger than the number of existing units, or in case of MPDs, simply larger than the number of existing units: `r nrow(redpropm.build)` parcels. *The choice of this factor greatly influences the results. We decided on value of 1 as it calibrates well when comparing results to our previous method.*

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# select households that live on the parcels with selected proposals
selhh <- hh[parcel_id %in% redpropm.build[, parcel_id]]
```

5. Extract households that live on those selected parcels. They correspond to the number of units that are at risk of displacement given the above conditions: `r nrow(selhh)`

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# output
res <- selhh[, .(HHatRisk = .N), by = parcel_id]
setkey(res, parcel_id)
res[pcl, `:=`(census_tract_id = i.census_tract_id, census_block_id = i.census_block_id)]

hhtot <- hh[, .N, by = "parcel_id"]
hhtot[res, hh_at_risk := i.HHatRisk, on = "parcel_id"][is.na(hh_at_risk), hh_at_risk := 0]
hhtot[pcl, county_id := i.county_id, on = "parcel_id"]

if(save.output){

    resall <- hhtot[pcl, .(parcel_id, county_id, census_block_id = i.census_block_id, 
                           census_tract_id = i.census_tract_id, hh_at_risk, hh_total = N), 
                        on = "parcel_id"][!is.na(hh_total)]

    fwrite(resall, file = paste0("hh_at_displacement_risk_age", age.limit, "_devfctr", comp.factor, 
                                 "-BY", BY, "-", Sys.Date(), ".csv"))
}
```

6. Export outputs on parcel level.

## Results

Here is a summary of the results.

* County level:

    ```{r echo = FALSE}
# summary
resout <- hhtot[, .(hh_at_risk = sum(hh_at_risk), hh_total = sum(N), 
                    percent = round(sum(hh_at_risk)/sum(N)*100, 1)), by = county_id]

merge(data.table(county_id = c(33, 35, 53, 61), county_name = c("King", "Kitsap", "Pierce", "Snohomish")),
                resout)
```

* Regional total:

    ```{r echo = FALSE}
# total
hhtot[, .(hh_at_risk = sum(hh_at_risk), hh_total = sum(N), percent = round(sum(hh_at_risk)/sum(N)*100, 1))]
```

## Neighborhood Measures

```{r echo = FALSE}
buffer.radius <- 660 # in feet (1/8 mile)
min.neighbors <- 5
size.breaks <- c(0, 2, 4, 6, 19, Inf)
size.labels <- c("1-2", "3-4", "5-6", "7-19", "20+")

# all residential parcels in the base year with their existing density (DU per acre)
nbpcl <- bld[residential_units > 0, .(DU = sum(residential_units)), by = parcel_id]
nbpcl[pcl, `:=`(census_block_id = i.census_block_id, parcel_sqft = i.parcel_sqft,
                x = i.x_coord_sp, y = i.y_coord_sp), on = "parcel_id"]
nbpcl[, size_class := cut(DU, size.breaks, labels = size.labels)]
nbpcl[parcel_sqft > 0, dens := DU / parcel_sqft * 43560]

# dominant size class per block
blkcl <- nbpcl[, .N, by = .(census_block_id, size_class)]
blkcl[, `:=`(n_pcl = sum(N), share = N/sum(N)), by = census_block_id]
blkdom <- blkcl[blkcl[, .I[which.max(share)], by = census_block_id]$V1,
                .(census_block_id, n_pcl, dom_class = size_class, dom_share = share)]
nbpcl[blkdom, `:=`(blk_n_pcl = i.n_pcl, blk_dom_class = i.dom_class, blk_dom_share = i.dom_share),
      on = "census_block_id"]

# aggregate density (total DU per total residential acre) of the other residential parcels in the block,
# i.e. excluding the parcel itself
nbpcl[!is.na(dens), `:=`(blk_n_nb = .N - 1,
                         blk_agg_dens = (sum(DU) - DU) / (sum(parcel_sqft) - parcel_sqft) * 43560),
      by = census_block_id]
nbpcl[blk_n_nb < min.neighbors, blk_agg_dens := NA]

# aggregate density of other residential parcels within radius of each parcel,
# using a grid with cell size = radius, so that all neighbors are in the 3x3 surrounding cells
buffer_density <- function(dt, radius, nchunks = 50){
    pts <- dt[, .(parcel_id, x, y, DU, parcel_sqft, cx = floor(x/radius), cy = floor(y/radius))]
    offsets <- CJ(dx = -1:1, dy = -1:1)[, k := 1]
    chunk <- cut(pts$cx, nchunks, labels = FALSE)
    rbindlist(lapply(split(pts, chunk), function(foc){
        cand <- foc[, .(fid = parcel_id, fx = x, fy = y, cx, cy, k = 1)][offsets, on = "k", allow.cartesian = TRUE]
        cand[, `:=`(cx = cx + dx, cy = cy + dy)]
        pairs <- pts[cand, on = c("cx", "cy"), nomatch = NULL, allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                     .(fid, parcel_id, DU, parcel_sqft, d2 = (x - fx)^2 + (y - fy)^2)]
        pairs[d2 <= radius^2 & parcel_id != fid,
              .(buf_n_nb = .N, buf_agg_dens = sum(DU) / sum(parcel_sqft) * 43560),
              by = .(parcel_id = fid)]
    }))
}
bufdens <- buffer_density(nbpcl[!is.na(dens)], buffer.radius)
nbpcl[bufdens, `:=`(buf_n_nb = i.buf_n_nb, buf_agg_dens = i.buf_agg_dens), on = "parcel_id"]
nbpcl[buf_n_nb < min.neighbors, buf_agg_dens := NA]

nbpcl[, `:=`(blk_rel_dens = dens/blk_agg_dens, buf_rel_dens = dens/buf_agg_dens)]

# mark parcels at risk in the base setting
nbpcl[, at_risk := parcel_id %in% res[, parcel_id]]

if(save.output)
    fwrite(nbpcl[, .(parcel_id, census_block_id, DU, size_class, dens, blk_n_pcl, blk_dom_class, blk_dom_share,
                     blk_n_nb, blk_agg_dens, blk_rel_dens, buf_n_nb, buf_agg_dens, buf_rel_dens, at_risk)],
           file = paste0("neighborhood_measures-BY", BY, "-", Sys.Date(), ".csv"))
```

These measures describe how similar the residential buildings in a neighborhood are, and where each parcel stands relative to its neighbors. They are computed for all `r nrow(nbpcl)` residential parcels in `r BY` (not only those passing the filters above), so that the neighborhood is complete.

* **Dominant size-class share** (`blk_dom_share`): Parcels are classified by the number of their existing DUs into `r paste(size.labels, collapse = ", ")`. For each census block, it is the share of residential parcels in the most common class (`blk_dom_class`). A value of 1 means all residential parcels in the block are in the same class.
* **Relative density**: The parcel's density (DU per acre) divided by the aggregate density of the *other* residential parcels in the same census block (`blk_rel_dens`) or with centroids within a `r buffer.radius` ft buffer around the parcel centroid (`buf_rel_dens`). The aggregate density is the total number of DUs of these parcels divided by their total area. Unlike a median over parcels, it reflects the size of large buildings, e.g. a single family house surrounded by many single family houses and a few large apartment buildings is less dense than its neighborhood. Values below 1 mean the parcel is less dense than its neighbors. It is set to missing if there are fewer than `r min.neighbors` neighbors, or if the parcel has zero area (`r nbpcl[is.na(dens), .N]` parcels).

For each parcel, the measures are saved in a csv file with the prefix `neighborhood_measures`. The tables below compare parcels at risk in the base setting (age limit `r age.limit`, redevelopment factor `r comp.factor`) with the remaining residential parcels.

* Distribution of parcels by the dominant size-class share of their block:

    ```{r echo = FALSE}
nbpcl[, dom_share_cat := cut(blk_dom_share, c(0, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99, 1), include.lowest = TRUE)]
dcast(nbpcl[, .N, by = .(risk = ifelse(at_risk, "pct_at_risk", "pct_not_at_risk"), dom_share_cat)][,
            percent := round(N/sum(N)*100, 1), by = risk],
      dom_share_cat ~ risk, value.var = "percent")[order(dom_share_cat)]
```

* Distribution of relative density:

    ```{r echo = FALSE}
nbpcl[, .(parcels = .N,
          blk_q25 = quantile(blk_rel_dens, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), blk_median = median(blk_rel_dens, na.rm = TRUE),
          blk_q75 = quantile(blk_rel_dens, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), blk_missing = sum(is.na(blk_rel_dens)),
          buf_q25 = quantile(buf_rel_dens, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), buf_median = median(buf_rel_dens, na.rm = TRUE),
          buf_q75 = quantile(buf_rel_dens, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), buf_missing = sum(is.na(buf_rel_dens))),
      by = at_risk][, lapply(.SD, function(x) if(is.numeric(x)) round(x, 2) else x)]
```

## Alternative Filters

```{r echo = FALSE}
filter_parcels <- function(age.limit = 8, dev.factor = 1, il.ratio = NULL, exclude.exempt = TRUE,
                           renters.only = FALSE, max.rel.dens = NULL, rel.dens.type = c("buf", "blk"),
                           max.value.per.unit = NULL, save = FALSE){
rel.dens.type <- match.arg(rel.dens.type)
rbld <- bld[residential_units > 0 & building_id %in% hh[, building_id] & year_built < (BY + 2 - age.limit)]

# exclude parcels that are tax exempt
if(exclude.exempt)
    rbld <- rbld[not_demolish == 0 & !parcel_id %in% pcl[exemption == 1, parcel_id]]

# keep only parcels where the improvement value of all buildings is less than il.ratio times the land value;
# parcels with missing (zero) land value cannot be evaluated and are kept
if(!is.null(il.ratio)){
    ilpcl <- bld[, .(impr = sum(as.numeric(improvement_value))), by = parcel_id][pcl, land_value := i.land_value, on = "parcel_id"]
    rbld <- rbld[!parcel_id %in% ilpcl[land_value > 0 & impr >= il.ratio * land_value, parcel_id]]
}

# keep only parcels where the density relative to the neighborhood (buffer or block) median is less than max.rel.dens;
# parcels with missing relative density (too few neighbors or zero area) are kept
if(!is.null(max.rel.dens)){
    rel.col <- paste0(rel.dens.type, "_rel_dens")
    rbld <- rbld[!parcel_id %in% nbpcl[!is.na(get(rel.col)) & get(rel.col) >= max.rel.dens, parcel_id]]
}

# remove parcels where the total (land + improvement) value per existing residential unit is larger than max.value.per.unit;
# parcels with missing (zero) land value are kept
if(!is.null(max.value.per.unit))
    rbld <- rbld[!parcel_id %in% tvpcl[land_value > 0 & DU > 0 & total_value/DU > max.value.per.unit, parcel_id]]

# select proposals that are on parcels with selected residential buildings
redprop <- dprop[parcel_id %in% rbld[, parcel_id]]
setkey(redprop, proposal_id, parcel_id)

# select buildings that are on parcels that have at least one proposal
redbld <- rbld[parcel_id %in% redprop[, parcel_id]]
setkey(redbld, building_id, parcel_id)

# sum existing DUs for each of the affected parcels
redpcl <- redbld[, .(DU = sum(residential_units)), by = parcel_id]
setkey(redpcl, parcel_id)

proptype <- cdprop[proposal_id %in% redprop[, proposal_id]][, 
                            .(is_res = any(building_type_id %in% c(19, 4, 12)), 
                                is_nonres = any(!building_type_id %in% c(19, 4, 12))), by = proposal_id]
setkey(proptype, proposal_id)
redprop <- merge(redprop, proptype, by = "proposal_id")

# for non-res proposals, estimate the number of units as if the project would be MF residential
redprop[, units_est := units_proposed]
redprop[is_nonres == TRUE, units_est := round(units_proposed/1000)]

redprop[redprop[, .I[which.max(units_est)], by = parcel_id]$V1, is_max := TRUE]
redpropm <- redprop[!is.na(is_max) & is_max == TRUE]

# join with existing units
redpropm[redpcl, existing_units := i.DU, on = "parcel_id"]
# adjust re-development filter
redpropm.build <- redpropm[units_est > dev.factor*existing_units | (units_est > existing_units & parcel_id %in% mpd[, parcel_id])]

# renters are tenure 3 (rented) and 4 (occupied without payment of rent)
hhsel <- if(renters.only) hh[tenure %in% c(3, 4)] else hh
selhh <- hhsel[parcel_id %in% redpropm.build[, parcel_id]]

res <- selhh[, .(HHatRisk = .N), by = parcel_id]
setkey(res, parcel_id)
res[pcl, `:=`(census_tract_id = i.census_tract_id, census_block_id = i.census_block_id)]

hhtot <- hh[, .N, by = "parcel_id"]
hhtot[res, hh_at_risk := i.HHatRisk, on = "parcel_id"][is.na(hh_at_risk), hh_at_risk := 0]
hhtot[pcl, county_id := i.county_id, on = "parcel_id"]

if(save){

    resall <- hhtot[pcl, .(parcel_id, county_id, census_block_id = i.census_block_id, 
                           census_tract_id = i.census_tract_id, hh_at_risk, hh_total = N), 
                        on = "parcel_id"][!is.na(hh_total)]

    suffix <- paste0(if(!is.null(il.ratio)) paste0("_ilr", il.ratio), if(!exclude.exempt) "_withexempt",
                     if(!is.null(max.rel.dens)) paste0("_rd", rel.dens.type, max.rel.dens),
                     if(!is.null(max.value.per.unit)) paste0("_tvpu", round(max.value.per.unit/1000), "k"),
                     if(renters.only) "_renters")
    fwrite(resall, file = paste0("hh_at_displacement_risk_age", age.limit, "_devfctr", dev.factor, suffix,
                                 "-BY", BY, "-", Sys.Date(), ".csv"))
}

return(hhtot[, .(parcels = sum(hh_at_risk > 0), hh_at_risk = sum(hh_at_risk), hh_total = sum(N),
                 percent = round(sum(hh_at_risk)/sum(N)*100, 1),
                 renters_pct = round(selhh[, mean(tenure %in% c(3, 4))]*100, 1))])
}
```

* Age limit 50 years:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(filter_parcels(50))
```

* Redevelopment factor 2:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(filter_parcels(dev.factor = 2))
```

* Redevelopment factor 3:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(filter_parcels(dev.factor = 3))
```

* Age limit 50 years and redevelopment factor 3:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(filter_parcels(50, dev.factor = 3, save = save.output))
```

## Additional Filters

```{r echo = FALSE}
il.ratio <- 1
max.rel.dens <- 0.75
# total (land + improvement) value and existing residential units (all buildings) per parcel
tvpcl <- bld[, .(impr = sum(as.numeric(improvement_value)), DU = sum(residential_units)), by = parcel_id][pcl[, .(parcel_id, land_value)], on = "parcel_id"]
tvpcl[is.na(impr), `:=`(impr = 0, DU = 0)][, total_value := land_value + impr]
# threshold for total value per existing unit, as a quantile over the parcels considered in the base method
tvpu.quantile <- 0.95
tvpu.threshold <- quantile(tvpcl[parcel_id %in% redpropm[, parcel_id] & land_value > 0 & DU > 0, total_value/DU],
                           tvpu.quantile, names = FALSE)
```

The following optional filters can be added on top of the base setting (age limit, redevelopment factor and excluding tax-exempt parcels):

* **Improvement-to-land value:** Keep only parcels where the improvement value of all buildings is less than `r il.ratio` times the land value, i.e. the land is worth more than the structures on it. Parcels with missing (zero) land value are kept.
* **Relative density:** Keep only parcels whose density is less than `r max.rel.dens` times the aggregate density of the other residential parcels within the `r buffer.radius` ft buffer (`buf_rel_dens`) or in the same census block (`blk_rel_dens`), i.e. parcels that are less dense than their neighborhood. Parcels with missing relative density are kept.
* **Total value per unit:** Remove parcels where the total value (land plus improvements) divided by the number of existing residential units on the parcel is larger than $`r format(round(tvpu.threshold, -3), big.mark = ",")`, which is the `r tvpu.quantile*100`th percentile over the `r nrow(redpropm)` parcels in the region considered in the base method. *The aim is to exclude parcels with currently expensive homes, e.g. waterfront properties, whose residents are unlikely to be displaced even if the parcel is zoned for more units. Since the improvement value relates to the existing buildings, the value is divided by the existing (not proposed) units.* Parcels with missing (zero) land value are kept.
* **Renters only:** Count only renter households (tenure 3 and 4). The percentage is still relative to all households, i.e. it is the share of occupied units that are at risk and occupied by renters.

Each row of the tables below adds one filter to the base setting; the last row combines all of them. The column `renters_pct` is the share of renters among households at risk. In the region, `r round(hh[, mean(tenure %in% c(3, 4))]*100, 1)`% of households are renters. The combination of all filters uses the buffer-based relative density. For each filter, a csv file with the suffix `_ilr`, `_rdbuf`, `_rdblk`, `_tvpu`, `_renters` or their combination is saved.

```{r echo = FALSE}
compare_filters <- function(age.limit, dev.factor, save = FALSE){
    rbindlist(list(
        cbind(filter = "base", filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor)),
        cbind(filter = paste("improvement/land <", il.ratio), filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, il.ratio = il.ratio, save = save)),
        cbind(filter = paste("rel. density (buffer) <", max.rel.dens), filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, max.rel.dens = max.rel.dens, rel.dens.type = "buf", save = save)),
        cbind(filter = paste("rel. density (block) <", max.rel.dens), filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, max.rel.dens = max.rel.dens, rel.dens.type = "blk", save = save)),
        cbind(filter = paste0("total value/unit < ", tvpu.quantile*100, "th pct"), filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, max.value.per.unit = tvpu.threshold, save = save)),
        cbind(filter = "renters only", filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, renters.only = TRUE, save = save)),
        cbind(filter = "all", filter_parcels(age.limit, dev.factor, il.ratio = il.ratio, max.rel.dens = max.rel.dens,
                                             rel.dens.type = "buf", max.value.per.unit = tvpu.threshold,
                                             renters.only = TRUE, save = save))
    ))
}
```

* Age limit 8 years and redevelopment factor 1:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(compare_filters(8, 1, save = save.output))
```

* Age limit 50 years and redevelopment factor 3:
    ```{r echo = FALSE}
print(compare_filters(50, 3, save = save.output))
```
